se_candidates.label: Classic gravity net flux (baseline A)
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = sum over j≠i of (T_ji − T_ij), with T_ij = κ * p_i^α * p_j^β / d_ij^γ

definitions.T_ij: Pairwise flow from i to j driven by node states and inverse power of distance. d_ij > 0 for i≠j.

assumptions_added_by_you: Treat the system as fully connected over distances with d_ii undefined and excluded.
If any d_ij = 0 for i≠j, replace by a small ε to avoid division by zero.

se_candidates.label: Single-constrained gravity (baseline B)
se_candidates.se_latex: SE_i = \sum_{j\ne i} (T_{ji} - T_{ij}),\quad T_{ij} = p_{i,t} \frac{p_{j,t} f(d_{ij})}{\sum_{k\ne i} p_{k,t} f(d_{ik})},\quad f(d) = d^{-\eta}
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = sum over j≠i of (T_ji − T_ij), with T_ij = p_i * [ p_j f(d_ij) / sum_k p_k f(d_ik) ] and f(d) = d^(−η)

definitions.f(d_ij): Power-law distance kernel f(d) = d^(−η), η>0

parameters.name: eta
parameters.meaning: Power-law decay of attractiveness with distance

assumptions_added_by_you: All destinations are available to each origin; exclude k=i from the normalization.
If any d_ij = 0 for i≠j, set f(d_ij) = f(ε) with small ε.

se_candidates.label: Distance-weighted diffusion (symmetric Laplacian)
se_candidates.se_latex: SE_i = \lambda \sum_{j\ne i} W_{ij} (p_{j,t} - p_{i,t}),\quad W_{ij} = K(d_{ij}),\quad K(d) = d^{-\eta}
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = λ * sum over j≠i of W_ij * (p_j − p_i) with symmetric weights W_ij = d_ij^(−η)

definitions.w_ij: Not used (unnormalized symmetric weights W_ij = K(d_ij))

se_candidates.difference_from_gravity_baselines: Linear diffusion driven by symmetric distance weights; no multiplicative mass terms or destination-choice normalization.
assumptions_added_by_you: Handle zero distances by replacing d_ij with ε > 0 in K(d).

se_candidates.label: Fractional nonlocal Laplacian
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = D_f * sum over j≠i of (p_j − p_i) / d_ij^σ
properties: enhanced long-range coupling vs. local diffusion
se_candidates.difference_from_gravity_baselines: A linear, nonlocal operator on state differences with heavy-tailed coupling; no OD flows proportional to p_i p_j.
assumptions_added_by_you: Exclude i=j; for very small distances, cap 1/d_ij^σ at 1/ε^σ.

se_candidates.label: Rank-based Zipf coupling
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = λ_z * sum over j≠i of W̃_ij * (p_j − p_i), with W̃_ij = 0.5*(r_ij^(−q) + r_ji^(−q)) where r_ij is the distance rank of j from i

definitions.N(i): r_ij is 1 for nearest neighbor, 2 for second nearest, etc.

parameters.name: q
parameters.meaning: Zipf-like rank exponent (higher q concentrates on few nearest)

properties: does not require metric scale, only order of distances
se_candidates.difference_from_gravity_baselines: Uses Zipf-like rank weights derived from distance ordering, not multiplicative masses or destination normalization.
assumptions_added_by_you: Break distance ties randomly or by stable indexing to define ranks.

se_candidates.label: Memory-concentrated kNN diffusion
se_candidates.se_latex: SE_i = \lambda_k \sum_{j \in N_K(i)} w_{ij} (p_{j,t} - p_{i,t}),\quad w_{ij} = \frac{K(d_{ij})}{\sum_{k \in N_K(i)} K(d_{ik})},\quad K(d) = d^{-\eta}
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = λ_k * sum over j in the K-nearest neighbors of i of w_ij * (p_j − p_i), with w_ij row-normalized within N_K(i) using K(d)=d^(−η)

definitions.w_ij: Row-normalized weights over the K nearest neighbors
definitions.N(i): N_K(i): the set of K nearest neighbors of i (by distance)

parameters.name: eta
parameters.meaning: Distance-decay exponent within the neighbor set

properties: asymmetric (row-normalized and kNN can be non-mutual)
captures concentration on few locations at high memory
se_candidates.difference_from_gravity_baselines: A kNN diffusion with neighbor-set truncation motivated by memory-driven concentration; no OD flow proportional to p_i p_j.
assumptions_added_by_you: K can be tuned; E3 suggests a regime change around ~20, so K≈10–20 is a plausible range.
If distances tie at the cutoff, break ties randomly to fix N_K(i).

se_candidates.label: Saturation-limited influence (capacity-inspired)
se_candidates.se_latex: SE_i = \lambda_s \sum_{j\ne i} w_{ij} \big( g(p_{j,t}) - g(p_{i,t}) \big),\quad w_{ij} = \frac{K(d_{ij})}{\sum_{k\ne i} K(d_{ik})},\quad K(d)=d^{-\eta},\quad g(p)=\frac{p}{1+p/\kappa}
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = λ_s * sum over j≠i of w_ij * (g(p_j) − g(p_i)), with w_ij row-normalized from K(d)=d^(−η) and g(p)=p/(1+p/κ)

parameters.name: kappa
parameters.meaning: Saturation scale (effective capacity) for influence at each node

properties: bounded influence at high p via g(p)
se_candidates.difference_from_gravity_baselines: Nonlinear, saturation-limited exchange on transformed states g(p); no multiplicative OD terms.
assumptions_added_by_you: Saturation scale κ is node-invariant; could be made node-specific using only distance-derived quantities if desired.

se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = ρ * p_i * sum over j≠i of w_ij * (A_j − A_i), where A_i = sum_k K(d_ik) is a distance-kernel accessibility and w_ij are row-normalized from K(d)
se_candidates.difference_from_gravity_baselines: Flows are biased by a distance-derived accessibility potential A, not by destination mass or gravity OD; multiplicative only in p_i.

se_candidates.label: Overlap-mixed local+global diffusion
se_candidates.se_latex: SE_i = (1-\Gamma)\, \lambda \sum_{j\ne i} W_{ij} (p_{j,t} - p_{i,t}) + \Gamma\, \chi\, (\bar{p}_t - p_{i,t}),\quad W_{ij}=K(d_{ij}),\quad K(d)=d^{-\eta},\quad \bar{p}_t=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k} p_{k,t}
se_candidates.se_plain: SE_i = (1−Γ) λ * sum over j≠i of W_ij (p_j − p_i) + Γ χ * (mean(p) − p_i), with W_ij = d_ij^(−η)

parameters.name: Gamma
parameters.meaning: Mixing weight between local (distance-based) and global (overlap-like) coupling

properties: captures dual-layer overlap as convex mixing
se_candidates.difference_from_gravity_baselines: A convex blend of symmetric distance-driven diffusion and uniform mixing motivated by layer overlap; no OD gravity proportional to p_i p_j.
assumptions_added_by_you: Interpret Γ as effective overlap between a distance-mediated layer and a well-mixed layer.
W_ij symmetric with W_ii=0; use ε for zero distances.
